intervention.change: Add min-p 0.1 truncation (tokens below 0.1 x the top token's probability are removed before sampling) to the plain-prompt base at T 1.0 / top-p 1.0; nothing else changes: no prefill, same cap, same seeds, one sample, no restart or vote.

cell.prompt: plain (the standard chat-template prompt, no prefilled tokens), as in the T3 cell
cell.seeds: per-request seed = the T3 cell's seed rule (base seed + problem_index), one sample per problem

intervention.count: Right answers over all 500 MATH-500 problems by grader v3 on the single sample; a cap-hit answer counts whatever v3 gives from its text, and an empty extraction counts wrong.

best_known.setting: base + cue, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, 4 samples, vote after restart with ties to the shortest finished sample (16,384 cap, grader v3)

intervention.why: The mechanism says the plain base's terse answers (about 60 % right at T 0.6, plain T 0.6 = 319/500) fail at T 1.0 because sampled tail tokens derail them after the opening, so cutting the tail at T 1.0 should bring the terse register back near its T 0.6 accuracy and lift the plain cell from 224 toward about 305, minus a few loops and cap hits that truncation brings back; the mode-selection rival expects only a small gain, from a higher self-open share.
